title: Bounded cleanup of a marked interval
statement: Let $w$ be a Boolean word, let $p$ be an input-head position for $w$, let $d$ be a data tape, let $\ell$ be an integer, and let $m,j$ be nonnegative integers. Assume $\ell\le 0$, $0<\ell+m$, $j<m$, and $d$ is blank outside $[\ell,\ell+m)$. Start the cleaner in state $0$ with data tape $d$, the marker true exactly on $[\ell,\ell+m)$, the origin marker at $0$, and all heads at $\ell+j$. There is a time $t$ with $0<t\le 3m+4$ at which it is in state $3$ with all three tapes blank and all heads at the origin.
replaced:
Let $d$ be a data tape blank outside an interval of width $m$ starting at $\ell$, with
$\ell \le 0 < \ell + m$, and let the heads start at $\ell + j$ for some $j < m$. Then
there is a positive time $t \le 3m + 4$ after which the interval cleaner, started in its
initial state on $d$, the interval marker, and the origin marker, is in its silent
return state with all three tapes blank and all heads at the origin.
